land.text: the counties of Anjou and Maine, which King John II gave to his son Louis in 1356 ('His father appointed him count of Anjou and Maine in 1356')

predecessors.note: A royal apanage. Cliopatria's County of Anjou row ends in 1332 and its County of Maine row runs 990-1481, so Maine overlaps this dossier's land.

land.text: the duchy of Anjou (reunited to the royal domain on René's death in July 1480) and Provence (bequeathed to Louis XI by Charles III on 10 December 1481)

successors.note: Provence was legally incorporated into the royal domain in 1486 (Provence page); a personal union until then.

land.text: the duchy of Bar, which René's will of 1474 left to his grandson René II, Duke of Lorraine

successors.note: Louis XI seized Anjou and Bar in 1474 (René page); the page does not say when Bar was returned. Cliopatria's 1482-1486 'Valois-Anjou' shape is this land.

capitals.name: Angers
capitals.note: Seat of the dukes: 'Seats: Chateau d'Angers, Chateau de Baugé' (House page); René's court at Angers from 1443 was 'one of the most brilliant in the kingdom of France' (Duchy page). Coordinates are the gazetteer's place Angers.

capitals.name: Aix-en-Provence
capitals.note: '1470 (Dec): ... René decided to move to Provence and left Anjou for good'; he left the duchy in October 1471 and died at Aix on 10 July 1480 (René page). Coordinates are the gazetteer's place Aix-en-Provence; the pages do not call Aix a capital.

rulers.name: Louis I
rulers.title: Count of Anjou and Maine 1356, Duke of Anjou 1360, Count of Provence 1382

rulers.name: Louis II
rulers.note: Died 29 April 1417; Yolande of Aragon administered Anjou.

rulers.name: Louis III
rulers.note: Died without children on 15 November 1434; Yolande was regent for him.

rulers.name: René
rulers.title: Duke of Anjou, Count of Provence; Duke of Bar from 1430 and of Lorraine from 1431

rulers.name: Charles IV
rulers.title: Count of Maine, Duke of Anjou and Count of Provence (Charles III of Provence)
rulers.note: Died without male heirs in December 1481 (House page infobox: dissolved 1481).

correction.text: the counties of Anjou and Maine from 1356; Anjou becomes a duchy on 25 October 1360

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1363. 'His father appointed him count of Anjou and Maine in 1356, and then duke of Anjou in 1360 and duke of Touraine in 1370.' Touraine is added in 1370, so 1356-1369 is Anjou and Maine only; the Duchy page says the county was 'roughly co-extensive with the diocese of Angers'.

correction.text: unchanged shape (Anjou, Maine and a band of Touraine, 23,450 km2), but it holds from 1370, when Louis I became duke of Touraine; for 1356-1369 use the Anjou-and-Maine keyframe

keyframe_review.note: 1363-1384 in Cliopatria. The shape is Anjou, Maine and a Touraine strip (about 0.2-1.3 E, 47-48 N) plus a southern band towards Thouars. The page dates the duchy of Touraine to 1370, not 1363. No infobox area on any page opened (Duchy page: 'the greater part of what is now the department of Maine-et-Loire').

correction.text: unchanged shape, 49,615 km2, with Provence including Nice, but holding 1382-1387 only: Louis I 'succeeded to the counties of Provence and Forcalquier' in 1382, and the separation of Nice and the Terres Neuves came in 1388

keyframe_review.note: 1385-1394 in Cliopatria; the Provence step is dated 1382 by the Louis I page, and in 1382-1387 the Union of Aix held eastern Provence for Charles of Naples ('Louis gained support in western Provence, while eastern Provence stayed loyal to Charles'), so the whole-Provence shape overstates control. The shape ends 1387 because 1388 took Nice, Puget-Theniers and the Tinee and Vesubie valleys away.

correction.text: unchanged shape, 46,000 km2 (Provence without Nice and the Alpes-Maritimes valleys), holding from 1388

keyframe_review.note: 1395-1401 in Cliopatria; the page dates the separation of Nice and 'the Terres Neuves de Provence' to 1388 (the city of Nice and its viguerie, Puget-Theniers, the Tinee and Vesubie valleys, placed under the House of Savoy), seven years before the shape drops them.

1402-1428, 45,953 km2: the same lands as 1395-1401. The Duchy page records Louis II's death on 29 April 1417 and Yolande of Aragon's regency 'for her son Louis III' who 'defended the duchy against the English', with no border change; unverified beyond that (page budget).

1429-1430, 32,377 km2: Anjou and Provence; the Maine cells are gone and Anjou is reduced (74% of Maine-et-Loire). Unverified: page budget; the Duchy page says only that Yolande 'defended the duchy against the English' and does not describe the English occupation of 1428-1448. Bar is added in 1430 (ledger).

union.text: the duchy of Bar, René's from 1430
the duchy of Lorraine, René's from 1431 though contested by Antoine de Vaudemont

correction.text: Anjou and Provence (32,058 km2) plus Bar from 1430 and Lorraine from 1431

keyframe_review.note: 1431-1439 in Cliopatria, without Bar or Lorraine. The René page: 'When Louis of Bar died in 1430, René inherited the duchy of Bar'; 'on his father-in-law's death, he succeeded to the duchy of Lorraine' (1431); defeated at Bulgneville in July 1431 and captured; released on parole in April 1432; title confirmed by Sigismund at Basel in 1434; ransomed about 1437. Cliopatria adds the eastern duchies only in 1440, so René's hold on them in 1431-1439 was nominal or contested, and the Lorraine step overlaps the Duchy of Lorraine row (1431-1768).

1440-1449, 63,319 km2 (Anjou, Provence, Maine, Bar and Lorraine, reaching Saarland and Luxembourg). Consistent with the René page (Bar 1430, Lorraine 1431, Anjou and Provence 1434) and with his return from captivity; no infobox area exists to compare. The Lorraine part overlaps the Duchy of Lorraine row, and the Saarland and Luxembourg cells go beyond the two duchies (about 36 cells of the 269 lie outside Anjou, Maine, Touraine, Provence, Lorraine and Meuse); the render order should settle the overlap.
1450-1452, 49,901 km2: the Maine cells (Mayenne, Sarthe) drop out. Unverified: page budget; the pages opened do not describe the county of Maine in these years.

1453-1481, 39,480 km2: Anjou, Provence and Bar; Lorraine is gone. The 1453 step is dated by the René page, which the earlier note misread: René's reign in Lorraine (jure uxoris, with Isabella) ran 25 January 1431 - 28 February 1453, and 'René now made over the government of Lorraine to his son John, who was, however, only formally installed as Duke of Lorraine on the death of René's wife Isabella in 1453' (infobox successor John II). No ledger event records the 1453 transfer yet (reviewer eu-10-h). The 1474-1476 seizure by Louis XI is in the ledger as an occupation of Anjou and does not change the shape.

correction.text: not Valois-Anjou land: Anjou reverted to the crown on René's death in July 1480, Provence was bequeathed to Louis XI in December 1481, and Bar (the Meuse and western Lorraine cells of this shape) was left by René's will to his grandson René II, Duke of Lorraine; use the Duchy of Lorraine row

keyframe_review.note: 1482-1486 in Cliopatria (7,149 km2, the Barrois). The House page's infobox dissolves the house in 1481; the Duchy page: 'Louis XI again added Anjou to the royal domain' in 1480; the Provence page dates the bequest to 10 December 1481. No Angevin land remains from 1482.

region.text: the counties of Anjou and Maine

ledger.note: 1356: King John II gives Anjou and Maine to his son Louis, founding the house. 'His father appointed him count of Anjou and Maine in 1356' (Louis I page); 'In 1356, Philip's son and heir, king John II, gave the County of Anjou to his son Louis' (House page). The Duchy page dates the gift to 22 August 1350, which conflicts.
25 October 1360: Louis I's county of Anjou is raised by letters patent to 'a duchy in the peerage of France'.

region.text: the duchy of Touraine, held by Louis I from 1370

ledger.note: 1370: Louis I becomes duke of Touraine ('duke of Anjou in 1360 and duke of Touraine in 1370'). The page names the title, not the extent of the land; Cliopatria's shape carries only a strip of Touraine, and the page does not say when the duchy was lost.

region.text: the counties of Provence and Forcalquier

ledger.note: 1382: Louis I succeeds Joanna I in Provence. 'In 1382, as the adopted son of Joanna I of Naples, he succeeded to the counties of Provence and Forcalquier.' The adoption was proclaimed on 29 June 1380 (House page). The counterpart is Cliopatria's Capetian House of Anjou row (1250-1384), which holds Joanna I's lands.

region.text: Provence, where 'the Union of Aix (1382-1387)' of Charles of Naples's followers opposed Louis of Anjou; western Provence backed Louis, eastern Provence stayed loyal to Charles

ledger.note: 1382: the Union of Aix forms against Louis I. 'Louis gained support in western Provence, while eastern Provence stayed loyal to Charles of Naples.' The counterpart is Charles of Naples, standing for Cliopatria's Kingdom of Naples row (1285-1501); the page does not name that row.

region.text: the end of the Union of Aix (1382-1387)

ledger.note: 1387: the Union of Aix ends (the page gives the span '1382-1387', not how it ended). The next year's separation of Nice shows that eastern Provence did not return wholly.

region.text: the city of Nice and its viguerie, Puget-Theniers and the valleys of the Tinee and the Vesubie, the Terres Neuves de Provence

ledger.note: 1388: Nice and the Terres Neuves de Provence pass under the House of Savoy (the dedition of Nice). 'This led, in 1388, to the separation of the city of Nice' and its viguerie, Puget-Theniers and the Tinee and Vesubie valleys, which 'placed themselves under the House of Savoy'; the upper Ubaye valley around Barcelonnette also came under Savoyard suzerainty (no date given).

ledger.counterpart: Duchy of Bar (Louis, Cardinal of Bar)
ledger.note: 1430: René inherits Bar. 'When Louis of Bar died in 1430, René inherited the duchy of Bar.' Cliopatria has no Bar row; the Meuse department stands for the Barrois (the real duchy also reached beyond it).

1431: René succeeds his father-in-law as Duke of Lorraine, but loses at Bulgneville in July 1431 to Antoine de Vaudemont ('backed by Burgundian forces') and is captured. 'on his father-in-law's death, he succeeded to the duchy of Lorraine'; paroled April 1432; Sigismund confirmed the title at Basel in 1434; ransomed about 1437. Cliopatria adds the land only in 1440, which fits the captivity. Month from the René page infobox: Duke of Lorraine (jure uxoris, with Isabella) 25 January 1431 - 28 February 1453 (month added by reviewer eu-10-h).

region.text: the duchy of Anjou, seized by Louis XI after René's will of 22 July 1474

ledger.note: 1474: Louis XI seizes Anjou. After René's will (22 July 1474) divided the succession between René II of Lorraine and Charles of Maine, 'King Louis XI then seized the duchy ... he did not keep it very long'. The René page says he 'seized Anjou and Bar' without a month.

region.text: the duchy of Anjou, restored to René

ledger.note: 1476: Louis XI reconciles with René and restores Anjou to him (Duchy page). The René page adds that the king tried in 1476 to force an exchange of the duchies for a pension; it does not say whether Bar was returned.

region.text: the duchy of Anjou, which Louis XI 'again added ... to the royal domain'

ledger.note: 10 July 1480: René dies at Aix and Anjou goes to the crown. 'René died, and Louis XI again added Anjou to the royal domain'; the infobox of the Duchy page gives 1482 for the integration. Charles IV of Anjou is listed for 1480-1481 (House page).

region.text: the duchy of Bar, left by René's will to his grandson René II, Duke of Lorraine

ledger.note: 1480: Bar passes to René II of Lorraine. The 1474 will left 'Bar to his grandson René II, Duke of Lorraine' and 'Anjou and Provence to his nephew Charles, count of Le Maine'; the year of the transfer is René's death (10 July 1480), the page does not date the handover itself.

region.text: Provence, the last Angevin land, bequeathed to Louis XI

ledger.note: December 1481: the last Angevin count dies and Provence goes to the crown. 'On December 10, 1481, Count Charles III of Provence dictated a will naming King Louis XI of France as his universal heir'; he died on the 11th and Forbin took possession on 19 December. The House page: 'Charles IV died without male heirs'; infobox dissolution 1481. Provence was legally incorporated into the royal domain in 1486.

wars.name: Union of Aix revolt in Provence

zones.text: eastern Provence, loyal to Charles of Naples

wars.outcome: The Union of Aix, formed in 1382 by followers of Charles of Naples, opposed Louis of Anjou; Louis held western Provence. In 1388 Nice and the Terres Neuves went to Savoy.
wars.note: The page gives the span '1382-1387' and not the course of the fighting; the Provence step in Cliopatria's 1385 shape therefore overstates control.

wars.name: Lorraine succession and the Battle of Bulgneville
wars.outcome: René was beaten at Bulgneville in July 1431 and captured; he was released on parole in April 1432 and Emperor Sigismund confirmed him as Duke of Lorraine at Basel in 1434.
wars.note: The page does not name the conflict as a war; the name is descriptive. It says Antoine de Vaudemont was backed by Burgundian forces.

wars.name: Angevin claims to the Kingdom of Naples
wars.outcome: Louis I invaded Naples in 1382 and died there in 1384; Louis II was crowned at Avignon in 1389 and lost to Ladislaus in 1399; René was King of Naples from 1435 and was driven out by Alfonso V in 1442. No French border moved.
wars.note: House page: 'Louis tried to secure Provence and invaded Naples, but died there in 1384'; 'In 1442, René was driven from Naples by Alfonso V of Aragon.' The map shows no Neapolitan land for this dossier.

wars.name: Louis XI's seizure of Anjou and Bar
wars.outcome: Louis XI seized the duchy after René's will of 22 July 1474 and restored it to René in 1476; Anjou went to the crown for good on René's death in 1480.
wars.note: The René page adds Bar to the seizure; the pages do not say when Bar came back.

certainty.note: Apanage and inherited lands: the Duchy page gives Anjou only as 'roughly co-extensive with the diocese of Angers'; Provence's eastern frontier was the Union of Aix front in 1382-1387 and the Savoyard line from 1388. No page opened gives a treaty or survey line.

sources.title: House of Valois-Anjou
sources.note: Identity, 1356 foundation, adoption 1380, Naples campaigns, 1480-1481 reversion; thin on Maine, Lorraine and Bar.

sources.title: Rene of Anjou
sources.note: Bar 1430, Lorraine 1431 and Bulgneville, Anjou and Provence 1434, Naples 1435-1442, the 1474 will, Louis XI's seizure, death 10 July 1480.

sources.title: County of Provence
sources.note: Union of Aix 1382-1387, the dedition of Nice 1388, the bequest of 10 December 1481 and the 1486 incorporation; asked twice (same page).

sources.title: Louis I, Duke of Anjou
sources.note: Count of Anjou and Maine 1356, duke 1360, Touraine 1370, Provence 1382, death 20 September 1384.

sources.title: Duchy of Anjou
sources.note: Duchy erected 25 October 1360, the dukes' dates, Louis XI's seizure 1474-1476, the reunion 1480; says nothing on the English occupation of 1428-1448.

notes: Cliopatria's House of Valois-Anjou is the Angevin cadet house's whole domain: Anjou and Maine, Provence from 1382, Bar and Lorraine from 1430-1431, in one row, so it overlaps the County of Maine row (990-1481), the County of Touraine row, the Duchy of Lorraine row (1431-1768) and Cliopatria's Capetian House of Anjou (1250-1384, Joanna I's Provence). Page budget (5) is spent: the 1402, 1429, 1450 and 1453 keyframes are kept as drawn and unverified. The English occupation of Anjou and Maine in the 1420s-1440s, the county of Maine under Charles of Maine, and John of Calabria's Lorraine after 1453 are not on any page opened, so no event is recorded for them (they explain the 1429, 1450 and 1453 steps if a gap-filler opens the Hundred Years' War and Duchy of Lorraine pages). Angevin Naples (1382-1384, 1387-1399, 1435-1442) is not drawn; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Naples and House of Anjou-Sicily rows cover it. The Duchy page dates the gift of Anjou to 22 August 1350 against 1356 on the House and Louis I pages (1356 used). The Duchy of Bar has no Cliopatria row and no dossier (counterparts_needing_dossiers); the Meuse department stands for it in region specs. The 1482-1486 shape is not Valois-Anjou land. Coordinates are the gazetteer's. No area figure appears on any page opened.
